title: Batch Pilot: incremental profiling, heuristic blending, and rollback-safe rollout
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Objective:
Build a 'Batch Pilot' capability that continuously profiles live workloads, composes multiple lightweight heuristics into a blended batching policy, and performs staged safe-apply rollouts with automatic rollback on quality or latency regressions. The goal is measurable cost reduction (tokens/GPU-hour) for workloads with heterogeneous arrival patterns while preserving 99th-percentile latency SLOs and model output quality.

Background and motivation:
- Existing autotune and batch recommendation tickets focus on offline profile generation or single-heuristic apply pipelines. We need a single runtime-friendly controller that can: (1) gather incremental workload signatures with low overhead, (2) evaluate multiple heuristic candidates in parallel (e.g., microburst-tolerance, KV-window-aware, cost-prioritized), and (3) apply parameter changes gradually with canarying, shadow evaluation, and automatic rollback.
- Teams consuming this feature: Hosted API, Dedicated autoscaler, Console rollout dashboards, and Solutions engineering (customer consults).

Design overview:
1) Incremental profiler: lightweight per-route fingerprinting to track sequence-length distributions, KV hit-rate proxies, inter-arrival bursts, and latency baseline. Profiles are aggregated into sliding windows (1m/10m/1h) with decay so the profiler adapts but resists noise. Stored signatures are compact (histogram + 3 scalar signals) to avoid DB bloat.
2) Heuristic blender: each heuristic provides a candidate (batch_size, max_wait_ms, kv_window) and a short probabilistic score computed from cost and SLO signals. We blend candidates using a tunable weight vector (alpha_t) that evolves via hill-climb with a safety margin.
3) Continuous safe-apply: rollout stages: shadow -> canary (1%) -> ramp (10/25/50%) -> full. Each stage runs paired control vs candidate comparisons for token cost, p99 latency, and quality regression measured via sentinel prompts. If any signal exceeds threshold, we auto-rollback and mark the candidate as 'rejected' until manual review.
4) Telemetry and explainability: every apply records the candidate snapshot, blended weights, decision reasons, and metrics. Console displays per-route batch recomms with expected cost delta and confidence score.

Implementation milestones:
- M1 (Week 1-2): Incremental profiler and compact signature store. (PR: draft, local integration tests).
- M2 (Week 3): Heuristic library (microburst-tolerant, kv-aware, latency-conservative, cost-first) + blending function lib.
- M3 (Week 4-5): Safe-apply orchestration (shadow/canary/ramp) with rollback hooks and sentinel evaluation harness.
- M4 (Week 6): Console integration: recommendation cards, expected savings, override UI.

Operational guardrails and safety checks:
- Minimal overhead requirement: profiler CPU < 0.5% on runtime nodes.
- Rollback triggers: p99 latency worsen > 10% absolute or quality sentinel fails > 1% regression; cost regressions allowed up to 2% for experimental runs.
- Manual approval gate for routes serving > $X/day.

Notes on uniqueness and scope control:
- This ticket focuses on the controller and safe-apply plumbing. It intentionally avoids building a full ML model for batching; heuristics + blend weights are faster to iterate and debuggable. Future work can add a learned candidate ranker.

acceptance_criteria: Profiler emits compact route signatures every 1 minute with <0.5% CPU overhead on a representative node
Heuristic library returns at least 4 diverse candidate configs per route with normalized score vector
Safe-apply pipeline supports shadow, canary, ramp stages and auto-rollbacks triggered by p99/quality thresholds
Console shows per-route expected cost delta and confidence; operations can force-apply or pause automated rollouts
End-to-end integration test demonstrating non-trivial cost reduction (>=8% tokens/GPU-hour) on synthetic mixed-burst workload without violating p99 SLO
